readme_locators.synchronization: L135; onboard channels interpolated onto the Vicon time base

reproduction: python r2-nanobench-derive.py SOURCE_DIRECTORY OUTPUT.csv.gz; inputs bound by sibling nanobench-provenance.json; filenames and acquisition URLs are listed there.

fields.trial: Original recording stem, not an independent aircraft identifier.
fields.relative_time_s: Original host time t minus that recording’s first t, computed in decimal seconds.
fields.motor_pwm_mean: Arithmetic mean of four motor commands in publisher PWM units (nominal 0 through 65535).
fields.motor_pwm_range: Maximum of the four PWM commands minus their minimum at this row.
fields.position_difference_norm_m: Unaligned Euclidean distance, in metres, between released concurrent Vicon position and Vicon-aided onboard EKF position in the Vicon frame.
fields.motor_state: four_commands_zero, any_command_nonzero or missing_pwm; this describes logged commands only.
fields.missing_columns: Missing or nonfinite source field names delimited by |; empty when all fields used are finite.

limits: Positions share a reference frame and Vicon observations were fused by the onboard filter. This difference measures internal consistency, not performance against an independent reference.

PWM commands are resampled inputs; zero commands do not directly measure rotor speed or physical stop. Motion-capture and onboard signals were time-aligned offline; 100 Hz tabular rows do not imply 100 Hz independent measurements in every channel.
The two multisine recordings use CF_01. The 211-row oval recording contains only four-zero commands and spans about 2.10 s despite a nominal 30 s configuration; no completed oval is evidenced.
No imputation, row removal, target-velocity inference or coordinate realignment was applied.
checks: Recomputed twice in Python standard library with byte-identical gzip output.
Compared all 17,118 derived rows against original source ordering, decimal relative time, every PWM status and feature, and every Euclidean position distance with separate row-wise code.
